title: The ram, the goat and the four kingdoms (Dan 8:3–8, 20–22)
speaker: Gabriel
description: The kings of Media and Persia are overthrown by the king of Greece, whose first king is broken and replaced by four kingdoms of lesser power.
in_text_interpretation: Explicit: ram = the kings of Media and Persia; goat = the king of Greece; great horn = the first king; four horns = four kingdoms from his nation (8:20–22).

interpretations.label: Alexander the Great and his successors
interpretations.framework: Common to traditional and critical interpreters
proponents: Josephus (Ant. 11.8.5, Alexander told he was meant)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the text itself names Media, Persia and Greece; Alexander, the first Macedonian king of Asia, defeated Darius III (Arbela, 331 BC) and died young; his empire passed to successors. Objections/variants: the four are listed differently — Jerome: Ptolemy, Philip Arrhidaeus, Seleucus, Antigonus; Guzik: Cassander, Lysimachus, Seleucus, Ptolemy (the coalition against Antigonus, Diodorus 20.106). Acceptance: no dissent found among the sources consulted on the identification of the great horn with Alexander.

referents.referent: The kingdoms of Alexander's successors (lists differ)
